---

# D1 — First choice

**Decision.** Store everything as markdown. The second sentence explains it.

**Why.** Files are diffable.

Topic: [[decisions/topic-architecture|Cross-cutting architecture]].

=== data/decisions/d2-second-choice.md ===
---
type: Decision
title: "D2 — Second choice: the CLI"
description: The CLI prints JSON when asked.
tags: [client-configurator]
provenance: [docs/decisions/D2-second-choice.md]
origin: external
source_url: "https://github.com/BeppeTemp/cartographer/blob/v1.2.3/docs/decisions/D2-second-choice.md"
---

# D2 — Second choice: the CLI

**Decision.** The CLI prints JSON when asked.

**Why.** It follows D1, which stored markdown, and D2 itself is not cited by its own concept.

Topic: [[decisions/topic-client-configurator|CLI and providers]].

Decisions cited: [[decisions/d1-first-choice|D1]]

# Architecture

How the parts fit together.

## Sections

- [[internals-contributing/arch/layers|Architecture — Layers]] — The layers are described below, one per sub-section, and together they are larger than the lowered cap.
  - [[internals-contributing/arch/layers-storage|Architecture — Layers — Storage]] — Storage keeps markdown files in a git repository.
  - [[internals-contributing/arch/layers-transport|Architecture — Layers — Transport]] — Transport carries requests over stdio or HTTP.
  - [[internals-contributing/arch/layers-indexing|Architecture — Layers — Indexing]] — Indexing builds an inverted keyword index in memory when the server starts.
- [[internals-contributing/arch/long-prose|Architecture — Long prose (part 1)]] — The first paragraph of a section that has no sub-headings but is longer than the hard cap, so it is cut at blank lines.
- [[internals-contributing/arch/long-prose-part-2|Architecture — Long prose (part 2)]] — The second paragraph keeps going with plain sentences about nothing in particular, only to take space in the part it lands in, and it ends here.
- [[internals-contributing/arch/long-prose-part-3|Architecture — Long prose (part 3)]] — The third paragraph follows the table.
- [[internals-contributing/arch/unsplittable|Architecture — Unsplittable]] — One single paragraph that no blank line can cut: it is the block the split leaves whole, and the size test names it.

=== data/internals-contributing/arch/layers-indexing.md ===
---
type: DocSection

tags: [arch, internals-contributing]
provenance: [docs/arch.md]
origin: external
source_url: "https://github.com/BeppeTemp/cartographer/blob/v1.2.3/docs/arch.md#indexing"
---

# Architecture — Layers — Indexing

Indexing builds an inverted keyword index in memory when the server starts. It is rebuilt after each write, which keeps search consistent with the files.

Part of [[internals-contributing/arch|Architecture]].

=== data/internals-contributing/arch/layers-storage.md ===
---
type: DocSection
title: Architecture — Layers — Storage
description: Storage keeps markdown files in a git repository.
tags: [arch, internals-contributing]
provenance: [docs/arch.md]
origin: external
source_url: "https://github.com/BeppeTemp/cartographer/blob/v1.2.3/docs/arch.md#storage"
---

# Architecture — Layers — Storage

Storage keeps markdown files in a git repository. Every write is a commit, and every commit is revertible, so history is never lost. Readers never see a half-written file.

Part of [[internals-contributing/arch|Architecture]].

=== data/internals-contributing/arch/layers-transport.md ===
---
type: DocSection
title: Architecture — Layers — Transport
description: Transport carries requests over stdio or HTTP.
tags: [arch, internals-contributing]
provenance: [docs/arch.md]
origin: external
source_url: "https://github.com/BeppeTemp/cartographer/blob/v1.2.3/docs/arch.md#transport"
---

# Architecture — Layers — Transport

Transport carries requests over stdio or HTTP. Both share one handler, so a request behaves the same on either. Authorization sits in front of the handler.

Part of [[internals-contributing/arch|Architecture]].

# Architecture — Layers

The layers are described below, one per sub-section, and together they are larger than the lowered cap.

## Subsections

- [[internals-contributing/arch/layers-storage|Architecture — Layers — Storage]] — Storage keeps markdown files in a git repository.
- [[internals-contributing/arch/layers-transport|Architecture — Layers — Transport]] — Transport carries requests over stdio or HTTP.
- [[internals-contributing/arch/layers-indexing|Architecture — Layers — Indexing]] — Indexing builds an inverted keyword index in memory when the server starts.

Part of [[internals-contributing/arch|Architecture]].

# Architecture — Long prose (part 2)

The second paragraph keeps going with plain sentences about nothing in particular, only to take space in the part it lands in, and it ends here. The sentence is padded so that this paragraph is a fair share of the section and the greedy grouping has something to place.

| Column | Value |
|---|---|
| a | one |
| b | two |
| c | three |
| d | four |

Part of [[internals-contributing/arch|Architecture]]. Part 2 of 3. Previous: [[internals-contributing/arch/long-prose|Architecture — Long prose (part 1)]]. Next: [[internals-contributing/arch/long-prose-part-3|Architecture — Long prose (part 3)]].

=== data/internals-contributing/arch/long-prose-part-3.md ===

type: DocSection
title: Architecture — Long prose (part 3)
description: The third paragraph follows the table.
tags: [arch, internals-contributing]

origin: external
source_url: "https://github.com/BeppeTemp/cartographer/blob/v1.2.3/docs/arch.md#long-prose"
---

# Architecture — Long prose (part 3)

The third paragraph follows the table. A table is never cut in the middle, because a break before a table row is not a break.

The fourth paragraph is the last one of this section and it closes the fixture with a few more words so that a third part exists. Another sentence follows only to add bytes to the last part of the section, which has to be long enough to stand next to the table on its own.

Part of [[internals-contributing/arch|Architecture]]. Part 3 of 3. Previous: [[internals-contributing/arch/long-prose-part-2|Architecture — Long prose (part 2)]].

# Architecture — Long prose (part 1)

The first paragraph of a section that has no sub-headings but is longer than the hard cap, so it is cut at blank lines. It goes on for a while to take some room in the unit.

# The Kb-a guide — Install (v1)

Run the installer. It needs nothing else: no database, no daemon and no account. The installer writes one binary into a folder on the path, and it can be removed by deleting that file again.

```sh
# this is a comment in a fence, not a heading
kb-a install
```

## Subsections

- [[using-cartographer/guide/install-v1-usage|The Kb-a guide — Install (v1) — Usage]] — Run kb-a run.
- [[using-cartographer/guide/install-v1-usage-2|The Kb-a guide — Install (v1) — Usage]] — A second heading with the same text.

Part of [[using-cartographer/guide|The Kb-a guide]].

=== instructions.md ===

perimeter: docs

# How to use this KB

This is the documentation of Cartographer v1.2.3, written as a knowledge base: ask it how Cartographer works and why.
Search it, read the concepts it returns and cite the concept ids you answer from. A page is a concept and its sections are `<page>/<section>`; a decision is `decisions/d<n>-<slug>`.

=== paths.yaml ===
paths:
  claude-home: {description: cited in the documentation as an example of the placeholder syntax}
